rule.quoted: All care must be obtained at the Yale Health Center at 55 Lock Street unless it is an emergency situation or you have a referral with prior authorization to see an outside clinician for services.
rule.differs: The page, read again, ends the sentence “to see an outside clinician for services.”; the research file had quoted it as ending “to see an outside clinician.”. The quote was corrected to the page; the rule is the same. The page also says Yale Health covers a student outside Connecticut only for “emergency care, acute care and pre-authorized short-term follow-up care”, which is why SLATE applies the rule only in a town that keeps Yale Health's practice (New Haven).

changes.what: For a visit with no practice of their own (or one that no longer sees them), the practice of the cover they're a member of, where the town keeps one: a Yale Health member with nothing picked is given Yale Health Center, Student Health. Somebody it doesn't cover still gets the first practice that sees anybody, Fair Haven. Until 2026-10-15 a member with nothing picked was given Fair Haven.

Whether a visit is had outside the practice the cover sends them to: Yale Health covering them at the moment, the practice not Yale Health's, in a town that keeps Yale Health's. A visit only; an emergency, urgent care and a stay aren't asked. SLATE keeps no referral with prior authorization, so none is honored (said in the comment).

A visit is priced at the practice it's had at (an optional clinicId, else their doctor then). Outside its practice, Yale Health's plan isn't read: the visit is the uninsured's, a provider's own self-pay price where it publishes one, else SLATE's price × 1.75 ($183.98 in 2026, $187.20 in 2027). Fair Haven publishes no fee and SLATE models no sliding fee for it, so it bills SLATE's uninsured price, as it does anybody uninsured. careQuote takes the practice too, for Papers' options.

Where the visit is had is worked out before its price. Outside the cover's practice, nothing goes toward Yale Health's out-of-pocket most, the bill carries no plan-paid part, and the notice says “Yale Health pays for a visit at its own Health Center, not here.” before the share. The care log keeps the visit's practice (careLog clinicId), and repriceCare prices it there again.

enroll.why: A played life with need now reaches a program renewal by the clock alone (the new need-paths journey). She is withdrawn, enrolled in HUSKY D on Papers, and her renewal on 1 November 2027 passes the income test on interest alone, then fails Connecticut's 2027 work test, so HUSKY D ends and the player is told. Nobody reaches a renewal that keeps a program. SLATE pays wages only for work-study and the Summer Cabaret, both a student's, while Yale Health covers her and Enroll is shut, so a life off Yale Health has no work for the work test. Covered Connecticut kept at a renewal needs last month's income between $1,835.40 and $2,327.50. The only way onto it is a personal leave without Affiliate cover begun after a month of five Fridays at the most work-study (October 2026, 5 × $414 = $2,070). That renews on 1 December 2027 on November's income: four Fridays, at most $1,656 at school and none on a leave, plus about $115 of interest, under $1,835.40. So it would end, not be kept, and that path (three months of every-evening work-study with coursework, a leave, thirteen more months) wasn't played. No income was invented and no eligibility loosened.

renewal.defect: Found 2026-10-15: at a program’s renewal (src/engine/systems/health.ts, healthMonth), a Covered Connecticut member whose last month’s income fell under HUSKY D’s 138% line got programFor() = medicaid, which wasn’t her program’s kind, so her cover ended with “Your Public Cover Ended At Renewal: Last month’s income is over what it allows.”, false (it was under). The reverse held too: a HUSKY D member whose income rose into Covered Connecticut’s band (138% to 175%) lost her cover with the same sentence. The same path ended New York’s Essential Plan and Medicaid members the same way.
source: 42 CFR 435.916(f)(1)-(2), law.cornell.edu, read 2026-10-15: before ending eligibility at renewal the agency considers all bases of eligibility, and for somebody found ineligible for Medicaid determines potential eligibility for the other insurance affordability programs (435.1200(e)).

45 CFR 155.430(d)(2)(v), law.cornell.edu, read 2026-10-15: an exchange enrollee newly determined eligible for Medicaid, CHIP or a Basic Health Program leaves her plan the day before that eligibility begins.

renewal.fix: From 2026-10-15, a renewal that finds her income in her state’s other program renews her into it from the renewal’s own instant: the old record ends at that instant and a new one, set up as health.enroll sets one (kind, state, band, scope, and renewAt so many months on: six in Connecticut from 2027), begins at it. So there’s no gap, one program at a time, and no premium (neither program has one). The notice is “Your Public Cover Changed At Renewal”: into HUSKY D, “Last month’s income is under what HUSKY D allows, which takes the place of Covered Connecticut: you’re renewed into HUSKY D from November 1, 2027, with no gap and no premium.”; into Covered Connecticut, “Last month’s income is over what HUSKY D allows and within what Covered Connecticut does: …”. HUSKY D’s work test is read of the program renewed into (`still ?? prog`), so a move into HUSKY D from 2027 needs 80 hours or $580 of last month’s work; failing it, she’s told “Last month’s income is under what HUSKY D allows, which takes the place of Covered Connecticut, and Medicaid now asks for 80 hours’ work or $580.00 of earnings a month, and last month had neither.” Over every limit (programFor undefined), the old sentence stays.
